html:
The Kite Runner is the first novel of the Afghan-American writer Khaled Hosseini, published in 2003. It tells of Amir, the son of a rich man in Kabul, his friendship with Hassan, the son of his father's servant, and Amir's betrayal of Hassan when they are boys.

The story runs from the last years of the monarchy in the 1970s, through the Soviet invasion, when Amir and his father flee to California, to the rule of the Taliban, when Amir goes back to Kabul to make amends. Kite fighting, a winter game of Kabul boys, frames the plot. Hassan is a Hazara, a mostly Shia people long looked down on by the dominant Pashtuns, and that gap runs through the book.

Published two years after the American invasion of Afghanistan, it became a worldwide bestseller and a film in 2007. For many readers in the West it was a first look at Afghan life beyond the war news. Its story of exile echoes that of the millions in the Afghan refugee exodus.
